memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made pomegranates of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen around the hem of the robe. And they made bells of pure gold and attached them round the hem between the pomegranates. The bells and pomegranates alternated round the hem of the robe to be worn for ministering, as the Lord commanded Moses." - Exod 39:24-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Around the bottom of the robe, alternating all the way: a pomegranate, a bell, a pomegranate, a bell.

Two very different things. Pomegranates are fruit — silent, full of seeds, a picture of abundance and life. Bells are sound — heard, announcing, unmistakable.

The earlier instruction explains the bells' purpose: their sound would be heard when the priest entered and left the Holy Place (Exod 28:35). The people outside could not see him, but they could hear that he was still alive and still serving on their behalf.

That is a picture of assurance. They could not see into the sanctuary, but the sound told them everything was well.

We cannot see Christ interceding for us either. But we have far more than a bell — we have His word, His Spirit, and the empty tomb. He always lives to intercede (Heb 7:25).

And notice the pairing. Fruit and sound. Substance and testimony. God asks for both. Words without fruit are noise; Paul says that without love we are only a clanging cymbal (1 Cor 13:1). Fruit without words leaves people guessing why.

Alternate them all the way around the hem of your life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is your Christian life more sound than fruit, or more fruit than sound?
2. What fruit is God growing in you at present?
3. Where have you stayed silent when a word was needed?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, grow real fruit in me and give me courage to speak. Let my life have both substance and testimony. Amen.
